discipline: STRUCTURAL / STEELWORK (EQUIPMENT SUPPORT, PIPE-RACK & ACCESS STEEL)
name: Structural Steel & Pipe-Rack Steelwork

sequence.note: Detailing must resolve where pipe/tray/equipment supports land before fab.
Weld zones for field connections left bare for later field welding.

activities: transport to site laydown / marshalling yard
ground pre-assembly of trusses / modules / PAUs
sequence.note: Modular/PAU approach front-loads ground assembly to cut crane time at height.

activities: confirm foundation concrete reached design strength
anchor bolts / base-plate levels surveyed to tolerance
sequence.note: Erection cannot start until anchors are surveyed and released.

activities: final dimensional survey — plumbness, elevation, alignment
remove temporary bracing only after permanent bracing installed
stair treads, ladders, handrails / guardrails / toe-boards
sequence.note: Walking surface (grating/decking) goes in before edge-protection handrails.

activities: release frame for cladding, equipment loading & MEP support fixing

typical_relationships.before: foundation concrete cured & anchor bolts surveyed (civil_interface)
typical_relationships.reason: Columns cannot be set until the foundation reaches strength and anchor-bolt positions are surveyed and released.
Connections are completed only once members are positioned and temporarily braced.
Secondary members hang off a stable, plumbed primary frame.
Access platforms need the walking surface before edge protection is fixed.
The building envelope fixes to a completed, tolerance-checked frame.
Racks are the support structure for the pipes and trays they carry.
Weld zones must stay bare and be NDT-inspected before being coated over.
Elevated equipment needs its supporting structure signed off before loading.

interfaces.requirement: Anchor bolts set to survey tolerance and foundations at design strength before erection.
Pipe-rack steel erected and aligned before rack piping and pipe supports.
Tray-support / rack steel in place before cable-tray installation.
Field welds inspected before final/protective coating; PFP applied after connections complete.
Supporting steel platforms complete before elevated equipment setting.
Steel structures bonded to the earth grid before energising mounted electrical equipment.

testing_requirements: Bolt torque / tension verification (turn-of-nut or TC-bolt) on completed connections
Field-weld NDT (visual, MT/UT/RT per weld class)
Dimensional survey — plumbness, elevation and alignment within tolerance
Coating DFT (dry-film thickness) and adhesion on field-applied coats
Grout compressive strength under base plates
Passive fire-protection (PFP) thickness check where applied
commissioning_dependencies: Structure is not commissioned itself, but dimensional & bolt/weld sign-off gates release of the frame for cladding, equipment loading and MEP support fixing
Permanent bracing installed before any temporary bracing is removed (load-path completeness)
Steel earthing/bonding complete before energising mounted electrical equipment
typical_exceptions: Pre-engineered metal buildings (PEB) and fully modular PAUs compress fabrication & erection into large single lifts
Stainless / architecturally-exposed steel is a different trade/finish and out of scope
evidence: Cladding, secondary steel or equipment loading is scheduled before the primary frame it depends on is erected, bolted and survey-released — an unstable/unsupported sequence.
